class.name: PhysXBuildingFire3D
class.brief_description: Burns a wooden building room by room: flashover, flames out of the windows, burn-through and collapse.
class.description: Add it to a building and describe its rooms in [member rooms]: each is a fire compartment with a box, a fuel load and its openings (doors, windows, hatches). An opening that lies on another room's face is a door between the two. A room on fire grows as t² ([member growth_time] to 1 MW) and takes air through its open openings, which limits it to Kawagoe's 1.5 A√H MW. Its hot layer heats as McCaffrey, Quintiere and Harkleroad's correlation gives, and glass falls out at about [member glass_break_temperature]. It flashes over at Thomas's heat release; after that its fuel burns at [member heat_release_rate] per square metre of floor, and what the air inside cannot burn comes out of the windows as flames of Eurocode's length (EN 1991-1-2 Annex B). Once 70% of its fuel has burnt it dies down linearly. Its timber chars at 0.8 mm a minute in a fully developed fire; the fire burns through walls ([member wall_thickness]), floors ([member floor_thickness]) and the roof ([member roof_thickness]) into the rooms beyond, and the room collapses when its framing has lost [member collapse_share] of [member member_size]. A [code]PhysXDestructible3D[/code] [member target] breaks up as it does. Otherwise the target's meshes over each room (its ceiling, the floor above, its roof) sag as the framing chars, then fall in as rigid bodies when that room collapses, room by room, and their colliders go with them. Smoke runs ahead of the fire. A burning room's plume fills a smoke layer under its ceiling (Heskestad's entrainment), carrying soot at [member smoke_yield]. The layer comes down until it reaches the tops of the openings and flows out of them, through doors into the next rooms (which fill and smoke in turn) and out of windows and eaves. So grey smoke pours from a house minutes before any flames show. Fire spreads between rooms through doors (radiation from a hot layer, flames through once it flashes), through burnt walls and floors, from a room that collapses onto the one below, and from flames out of a window to the window above. Water puts it out. Water in a room boils off and takes 2.6 MJ per kilogram. Taking about a third of what the fire could release puts the flames down (about 0.15 kg/s per MW, as fire services find), and the steam pours out of the windows. A flashed-over room falls back to a growing fire, and it goes out if the water keeps winning for twenty seconds. A weaker stream only holds it back, and the fire grows again when the water stops. Half a millimetre of water on burning cladding puts it out, and wet cladding does not catch. It catches from outside. A [PhysXFireSpread3D] ([member fire]) burning at its walls, hot gas in [PhysXFlow3D], radiation from burning [PhysXBurnable3D] and other buildings, and piles of firebrands on its roof or at the foot of its walls all heat its cladding, which lights at a thick solid's ignition dose. The burning patch spreads over the face and lets the fire in where it reaches a window or burns through. A firebrand landing in an open window lights the room's contents about one time in five. It draws flames and smoke in the fire's [PhysXFlow3D] (or [member flow]): inside each burning room, smoke from the top of its openings before flashover, flames out of them after, through an open roof and on burning cladding. A light flickers at each room's fire, and the meshes under [member target] char with the [PhysXBurnable3D] look. It throws firebrands that can start spot fires and light other buildings, radiates to its neighbours, and reports its heat, plumes and smoke to [WorldFire].

method.name: add_brand
method.description: Rests a firebrand on the building at [param position] (a surface facing [param normal]); [param glow] is how much of it is left (0 to 1). In an open opening it lands on the room's contents. Elsewhere it piles on the roof or at the foot of the wall it hit, and heats the cladding there. Firebrands call this when they land on a collider under [member target].

method.name: apply_water
method.description: Puts [param kg] of water on the building at a global [param position], from a hose, a bucket brigade or a script. It goes into the room there, or through an open window near it, or onto the cladding of the nearest face. Liquid [PhysXParticleFluid3D] water inside a room or against its walls counts by itself.

method.name: extinguish
method.description: Puts out every room and the cladding.

method.name: get_broken_windows
method.description: How many glazed openings have lost their glass.

method.name: get_firebrand_count
method.description: Firebrands it has in flight.

method.name: get_heat_release
method.description: The whole building's heat release in kW: its rooms, the flames outside them and the burning cladding.

method.name: get_ignition_cause
method.description: What first set the building alight: [code]"direct"[/code] ([method ignite]), [code]"firebrand"[/code] (embers through an opening, or a glowing pile of them against the cladding) or [code]"heat"[/code] (radiation or flame contact from fires nearby). Empty until it catches.

method.name: get_ignition_time
method.description: Fire seconds from when it started stepping to its first catch (scaled by [member time_scale]), or [code]-1[/code] if it has not caught.

method.name: get_room_char_depth
method.description: How deep a room's timber has charred, in metres.

method.name: get_room_visibility
method.description: How far one can see in a room's smoke layer, in metres (3 / K for soot's extinction, Mulholland); 1000 when clear.

method.name: get_room_water_cooling
method.description: The heat in kW the water in a burning room takes as it boils off.

method.name: get_room_count
method.description: The number of rooms.

method.name: get_room_flashover_time
method.description: Seconds from a room's ignition to its flashover, or -1 if it has not flashed over.

method.name: get_room_fuel_left
method.description: The share of a room's fuel left, 0 to 1.

method.name: get_room_heat_release
method.description: A room's heat release in kW, inside and out of its openings.

method.name: get_room_layer_height
method.description: Metres from a room's floor up to the underside of its smoke layer; the room's height when there is none, 0 when the room is full of smoke.

method.name: get_room_state
method.description: Where a room's fire is.

method.name: get_room_temperature
method.description: The temperature of a room's hot layer in °C.

method.name: get_shard_count
method.description: Pieces of window glass it has dropped (at most 300).

method.name: get_smoke_rate
method.description: Smoke particulate it gives off, in kg per real second ([member smoke_yield] of the fuel it burns).

method.name: get_spot_fire_count
method.description: Spot fires its firebrands have started.

method.name: get_visibility_at
method.description: How far one can see at a global [param position]: the room's smoke visibility if the point is in its layer, else 1000.

method.name: ignite
method.description: Starts a fire in the room holding [param position] (a global position), or the nearest room.

method.name: is_burning
method.description: Whether any room or any of its cladding is burning.

method.name: is_room_collapsed
method.description: Whether a room's framing has failed.

method.name: radiant_flux_at
method.description: The radiant heat at [param position] in kW/m² from every burning building: its open windows as panels glowing at the hot layer's temperature, and its flames outside and through open roofs. [PhysXBurnable3D] and cloth read it.

members.member: The share of a framing member's section charred away (from both sides) at which a room collapses.
A [PhysXFireSpread3D] whose flames heat the walls and whose ground the window flames and firebrands can light. Its [PhysXFlow3D] draws the flames unless [member flow] is set.
Firebrands a second per MW of fire once a room has flashed over (structure fires throw many: Suzuki and Manzello).
If [code]true[/code], it throws firebrands from its window flames and open roofs.
Metres of timber a fire chars through before it reaches the room above.
The [PhysXFlow3D] the flames and smoke are drawn in; empty uses [member fire]'s.

If [code]true[/code], it draws a pane of glass in each glazed opening, and when the heat breaks it the pane falls out as angular shards, pushed outward when the room is near flashover. Turn it off for a building whose meshes already have glass.
The hot-layer temperature in °C at which window glass falls out (each pane up to 80 °C later).
Seconds for a room fire to grow to 1 MW (300 is Eurocode's medium growth, for dwellings).
kW per square metre of floor a fully developed room fire releases when it has air enough (250 for dwellings).
Energy of each burning room's light at 1 MW; 0 for no lights.
The smallest side of its framing members, in metres.
Metres of roof a fire chars through before flames break out of it.

The rooms, as dictionaries: [code]box[/code] ([AABB] in this node's space), [code]fuel_load[/code] (MJ per square metre of floor, 780 by default, Eurocode's mean for dwellings) and [code]openings[/code], an array of dictionaries with [code]face[/code] (a [enum Face]), [code]rect[/code] ([Rect2] on the face in metres: along the wall from the room's lower corner and up from its floor; on the top, x and z) and [code]glazed[/code] ([code]true[/code] for a window with glass).
Kilograms of smoke particulate per kilogram of fuel burnt.
The building: its meshes char, its colliders take firebrands, and a [code]PhysXDestructible3D[/code] breaks where rooms fail.
Metres of timber a fire chars through before it reaches the next room, or the cladding before it reaches inside.

signal.name: ignited
signal.description: Emitted once, when the building first catches; [param cause] as [method get_ignition_cause].

constants.constant: Dying down, most of its fuel burnt.
